name: Keyboard Map (layout leak)
plain: Reveals the physical-to-printed key mapping, i.e. the keyboard layout.
meaning: Shows which keyboard layout the person uses (QWERTY, AZERTY, Dvorak, language), a strong locale and fingerprint signal. No prompt.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt; Chromium exposes it to secure contexts.
steps: Read KeyboardLayoutMap of key codes to characters

limits.headline: Can tell your keyboard layout, which hints at your country and language
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page or app loads
can: Check which character each physical key produces
Guess your language or region from that layout
Add to a profile of your device to help recognise you
cannot: Show a permission pop up; there is none
limits.differs: Only Chrome and Edge on desktop support it. Firefox, Safari and most phones do not.

story.what_it_is: Reveals which physical key makes which letter, so the page learns your keyboard layout.
story.for_you: You see nothing. The page quietly learns whether your keyboard is QWERTY, AZERTY, Dvorak or another layout. No prompt appears. It may be used to guess your country.
story.for_makers: Makers of games and editors use it for correct key labels. Fraud and tracking systems also use it as a free hint to your language, and in a fingerprint it adds a few bits of uniqueness.

use_cases.example: A browser game rebinds its movement keys to fit a Dvorak or AZERTY keyboard so players are not stuck with wrong keys.
A music web app maps piano keys to the correct physical row on any layout.
An ad network adds the layout to a profile and guesses a user's language when other signals are missing.
A fingerprinting script mixes layout, fonts and screen size to spot returning visitors.
A fraud engine flags an order that claims to be in Germany but types on a Russian layout.
A coding web app shows the correct shortcut key names for each layout.

legit_uses: Showing correct key hints in games
